_about: Public-domain T. De Witt Talmage (1832-1902), preacher of the Brooklyn Tabernacle and editor of The Christian Herald, for the Word Hoard: Crumbs Swept Up (1870), The Abominations of Modern Society (1872), The Brooklyn Tabernacle Sermons (1872), Around the Tea-Table (1874), Every-Day Religion (1875), New Tabernacle Sermons (1886) and From Manger to Throne (1893), from Internet Archive scans. Most of his sermon books were taken down by reporters and revised; each is flagged. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 36 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

tdtalmage-abominations: The Abominations of Modern Society (New York: Adams, Victor, 1872)
tdtalmage-tabernacle-sermons: Sermons delivered in the Brooklyn Tabernacle (New York: Harper & Brothers, 1872)
tdtalmage-every-day-religion: Every-Day Religion: Sermons Delivered in the Brooklyn Tabernacle, revised from phonographic reports (New York: Harper & Brothers, 1875)
tdtalmage-new-tabernacle: New Tabernacle Sermons, publication authorized (New York: E. B. Treat, 1886)
tdtalmage-manger-to-throne: From Manger to Throne, embracing a new Life of Jesus the Christ and a History of Palestine (Philadelphia: Historical Publishing Company, 1893)

_alternates.tdtalmage-copies: PG 13104 (Abominations, no publisher); PG 14139 (Munro's New Tabernacle Sermons, 1886); PG 14662 (a later Tea-Table); PG 22343 (The Wedding Ring, 1896); Old Wells Dug Out (London 1875; Funk & Wagnalls 1886)

_excluded.tdtalmage-other: T. De Witt Talmage as I Knew Him (1912, finished by Mrs. Talmage); anthologies; extract books compiled by others; books by James E. Talmage
